What we are practising

1. Draw and label a tree.
2. Convert links into row indexes.
3. Trace a small recursive traversal.
4. Complete and test InOrder.

The whole subtree matters

Each node has at most two children.
A leaf has no children.
A subtree includes its root and everything below it.

The BST rule applies to the entire subtree.

The empty subtree

When p = -1, return immediately.
Read no array cell. Output nothing.

A leaf still has two empty subtrees.

If p = -1 Then
    Exit Sub
End If

This is a deliberate change from the previous lesson, which checked child pointers before calling. Here the procedure accepts -1, so the starting tree can also be empty. Both are valid designs; use only this one today.
The in-order recipe

For the subtree at p:

1. If p = -1, return.
2. Do the whole left subtree.
3. Output this node’s data.
4. Do the whole right subtree.
5. Return to the caller.

Left, node, right applies at every node, not just the original root. Put your finger on the current rule. The caller pauses while a child call runs.
A leaf takes three calls

Start InOrder(1), where data = 3.
Its two child pointers are -1.

It calls InOrder(1).
The root call waits before its output.

After the left call finishes,

The complete in-order procedure

Each call gets its own local p.
The caller resumes after a child call.

Start with InOrder(RootPointer).

Sub InOrder(ByVal p As Integer)
    If p = -1 Then
        Exit Sub
    End If
    InOrder(TreeArray(p, 0))
    Console.WriteLine(TreeArray(p, 1))
    InOrder(TreeArray(p, 2))
End Sub

Reveal after Task 4. Gap answers: -1, Exit Sub, 0, 1, 2. With RootPointer=-1 there is no output and no array access. ByVal helps pupils see that each invocation has its own parameter value.
Two checks for broken code

Safety: does the -1 check happen first?
Order: is the output between the calls?

Check for -1
Call left subtree
Output current data
Call right subtree
Task 5A • Explain both bugs before repairing them
Task 5A: accessing row -1 before the guard crashes. Moving the guard first prevents that, but output first is pre-order, so the output also needs to move between the child calls.

title: Optional: records store the same fields

text: Optional: records store the same fields

A record groups the three integers.
Its child pointers still store indexes.
All child pointers must be initialised to -1.

Structure NodeRecord
    Public LeftPointer As Integer
    Public Data As Integer
    Public RightPointer As Integer
End Structure
Dim Nodes(3) As NodeRecord

' Array:  TreeArray(p, 0)
' Record: Nodes(p).LeftPointer

This is a record with fields only, no methods or constructors. VB.NET default integers are 0, so explicitly set both child pointers to -1. Optional booklet extension contains the translation task. No chapter 20 concepts are required.
